Git branching is a powerful feature in version control that helps teams work on different tasks simultaneously. Instead of everyone editing the same main code, developers create feature branches—separate copies of the project where they can add new features or fix bugs without affecting the stable version.

Once their work is complete, they merge their branch back into the main branch. This combines the changes, but first, most teams use pull requests to review the code. A pull request is a formal request to merge, allowing teammates to comment, suggest improvements, and catch problems before the code is added.

This workflow keeps the main project reliable, reduces conflicts, and ensures that every change is carefully reviewed. For both beginners and experienced developers, understanding branching is essential for smooth, collaborative coding.
